parts.text: Which claim correctly explains the difference after some time?

options.text: The lukewarm milk forms curd because the starter microbes work well at that warmth; the cold milk does not curdle in the same way.
Lukewarm milk turns into curd immediately when the starter is mixed in.
Only the cold bowl forms curd; the lukewarm bowl stays liquid because warmth inhibits the starter.
Milk kept boiling hot after adding the starter will form curd just as lukewarm milk does.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Mitali adds the same curd starter to a bowl of lukewarm milk and to a bowl of cold milk. She leaves both bowls for some time.

part_answers.answer: Starter microbes need lukewarm conditions and time to turn milk into curd; cold milk slows them and boiling heat harms them.

teacher.key_rationale: Lukewarm milk with starter forms curd over time; cold milk with the same starter does not. Immediate curdling, reversing which bowl works, or treating boiling milk as equal all miss that warmth-and-time hinge.
